scenario.name: Linux Kernel Cgroups Docs, Trail of Bits & Falco — Privileged Container CAP_SYS_ADMIN Cgroup v1 release_agent Audit
scenario.overview: Picture a brick university lecture and exam hall with tiered wooden student desks, a tall green chalkboard, hallway lockers, and a wooden proctor podium at the front. Inside the quiet university exam hall, a student slips hidden extra directions written in faint pencil into the margin of a submitted study booklet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the proctor podium & answer key folder. The university dean reviews the exam hall proctor log and flags an automated grading run that tried to access locked answer folders mid-session. In this scenario (T1611, Linux Kernel Cgroups Docs, Trail of Bits & Falco, Privileged Container CAP_SYS_ADMIN Cgroup v1 release_agent Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller, then enabling notify_on_release=1, then child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller, then Enabling notify_on_release=1, then Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1611 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Migrate nodes to cgroup v2 (unified hierarchy, which removes the legacy release_agent mechanism), drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN from all pods, and keep AppArmor/SELinux profiles enforced.

stages.title: Stage 2: Enabling notify_on_release=1 & Writing OverlayFS Host Path to release_agent
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: When the exam proctor at the front podium feeds that booklet into the automated grading helper, the hidden margin text overrides the proctor’s grading instructions. Here in Step 2 inside the university hall, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the locked registrar grade cabinet. Next, the follow-up artifact cat /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , cat /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exa so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Enabling notify_on_release=1 & Writing OverlayFS Host Path to release_agent" , The container creates a child cgroup , /tmp/cgrp/x, writes 1 into /tmp/cgrp/x/notify_on_release, and writes the resolved host OverlayFS path , /var/lib/docker/overlay2/<id>/diff/cmd into the root cgroup release_agent file while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ write("/tmp/cgrp/release_agent", "/var/lib/docker/overlay2/9a8b.../diff/diag.sh") / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Cgroup v1 Mount (/tmp/cgrp)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Kernel kthreadd / usermodehelper).

keySpecs.value: Enable the built-in Falco rule "Determines if a container writes to a cgroup release_agent file" to trigger an immediate critical alert and kill the offending container.

stages.title: Stage 3: Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Following the concealed instructions verbatim, the helper opens the answer-key folder on the podium and emails the exam sheet straight back out of the hall. In this final step inside the university hall, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the proctor podium & answer key folder until the exam hall proctor log catches the mismatch. When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup.procs and immediately exits, the Linux kernel cgroup1_release_agent workqueue invokes call_usermodehelper() in the root host namespace (PPID 2 kthreadd) to execute the release_agent path (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with ParentKernelThread=PPID 2 , kthreadd -> call_usermodehelper, ExecutedOverlayPath=/var/lib/docker/overlay2/9a8b/diff/diag.sh, HostNamespaceUid=uid=0 , root so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ps -ef --forest | grep kthreadd (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ps -ef --forest | grep kthreadd via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host" , When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -pp 2 -m SYSCALL -sv yes -i runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -pp 2 -m SYSCALL -sv yes -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the e so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host" , When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ /var/lib/docker/overlay2/9a8b/diff/diag.sh /x (spawned by kernel kthreadd PPID=2) / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 Cgroup v1 Mount (/tmp/cgrp)) to Node ④ (#4 notify_on_release & release_agent), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Kernel kthreadd / usermodehelper).

keySpecs.value: Audit all user-mode processes spawned directly by kernel thread PPID 2 (kthreadd / call_usermodehelper) whose executable path resides inside /var/lib/docker/overlay2/ or /run/containerd/.
